sections.title: Habit and habitat
sections.text: Briza maxima, the greater quaking grass, is an annual grass native to the Mediterranean region and Macaronesia, and now cultivated elsewhere. It grows about 20–70 cm tall. Its conspicuous, hanging, heart-shaped spikelets sway on slender stalks.

sections.title: Spikelets and uses
sections.text: It grows in open grassy places and is chiefly cultivated as an ornamental grass or dried for arrangements. The plate shows its characteristic large spikelets. It differs from the perennial Briza media, which is shorter and has smaller spikelets.
